content.comment_body: Good morning everyone. Is there a way to program two inputs such that both must be activated simultaneously? For instance, designing a cutting cycle where the operator is required to use both hands on the controls to ensure safety. I’ve experimented with multiple combinations of inputs, logic functions, and timers, but there still seem to be vulnerabilities. Any advice would be appreciated.
I might be misunderstanding, but it seems like you could use an AND logic block for this. Connecting both inputs so that output is triggered only when both are active could be a solution.
Please refer to the attached file.

Hello. Here’s one suggestion: [IMAGE] Note that proper implementation of two-hand control is more complicated and requires official certification. In this setup, both buttons have to be pressed within a specific time interval, which prevents bypassing safety by manipulating just one switch in a tricky manner (like using box sealing tape). Humans cannot activate both buttons at exactly the same time, so the timer is brief but realistically achievable. Would this approach suit your needs?
Dear [user_name], Safety must come first! [product_name] does not include certified safety outputs. Consider using a certified safety relay for proper two-hand monitoring.
After reviewing current regulations, it appears that a certified solution is necessary. Thank you to everyone for your input.

I’ve adjusted the program slightly. In the initial draft, output could be activated if both buttons were pressed during startup or due to another error causing both inputs to signal. With enhanced monitoring, both inputs are required to be off before initiating the sequence, which adds a layer of safety.

Interesting topic. As safety has become even more critical, I have replaced a custom-built relay with a certified relay for two-hand controls. This method processes the action by requiring movement with both hands on the push buttons, even though only one input is used on the relay—a solution implemented through specific hardware wiring.
